rules: Upon reset, all writable bits of the machine-level mstateen CSRs are initialized by the hardware to zeros.
If machine-level software sets any writable mstateen bits to nonzero, it must initialize the matching hstateen CSRs, if they exist, by writing zeros to them.
If any mstateen bits that are set to one have matching bits in the sstateen CSRs, machine-level software must also initialize those sstateen CSRs by writing zeros to them.
Software should ensure that all writable bits of sstateen CSRs are initialized to zeros when an OS at supervisor level is first entered.
Bit 63 of each mstateen CSR controls access to the matching sstateen and hstateen CSRs.
Bit 63 of each mstateen CSR may be read-only zero only if the hypervisor extension is not implemented and the matching supervisor-level sstateen CSR is all read-only zeros.
The C bit of mstateen0, hstateen0, or sstateen0 controls access to any and all custom state.
If misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of mstateen0 is read-only zero.
If misa.F = 0 and the FCSR bit of a controlling stateen0 CSR is zero, all floating-point instructions cause an illegal-instruction exception.
The IMSIC bit in mstateen0 controls access to the IMSIC state, including CSRs stopei and vstopei, provided by the Ssaia extension.
The AIA bit in mstateen0 controls access to all state introduced by the Ssaia extension and not controlled by either the CSRIND or the IMSIC bits of hstateen0.
The CONTEXT bit in mstateen0 controls access to the scontext and hcontext CSRs provided by the Sdtrig extension.
The P1P13 bit in mstateen0 controls access to the hedelegh introduced by Privileged Specification Version 1.13.
Upon reset, mnstatus.NMIE contains the value 0.
Software can set mnstatus.NMIE to 1, but attempts to clear mnstatus.NMIE have no effect.
Counting of cycle and instret events does not occur while executing in an inhibited privilege mode defined by mcyclecfg or minstretcfg.
Instructions that retire in an inhibited mode do not increment instret, unless they are xRET instructions originating from a non-inhibited mode.
If an instruction is emulated by software running in a privileged mode that is inhibited in minstretcfg, the emulation routine must emulate the instret increment.
